title: Invariance of cut size along a surviving run
statement: Let $s$ and $t$ be states of the contraction process, each consisting of a multigraph together with a distinguished cut, and suppose that $t$ is obtained from $s$ by a surviving run of length $n$, that is, by $n$ consecutive contractions of edges that do not cross the distinguished cut of the current state. Then the distinguished cut of $t$ has the same size as the distinguished cut of $s$, where the size of a cut is the number of its crossing edges counted with multiplicity.
hypotheses_covered: $t$ is reachable from $s$ by a surviving run of length $n$ (for some $n \ge 0$)
$s$ and $t$ are states (multigraph with a distinguished cut)
replaced:
If $t$ is reachable from $s$ by a surviving run of any length, then
$t.C.\mathrm{size} = s.C.\mathrm{size}$.
